steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to show what we know about fractions! We will answer questions about halves, quarters, equal parts, and fair sharing. Then we will think about what we have learned. Ready?
steps.studentText: Today we show what we know about fractions and think about our learning!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with a checklist and fraction shapes
media.fallbackText: Owl teacher waving hello with a checklist and fraction shapes

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn
steps.studentText: Today you will answer questions about fractions to show what you know. Then you will think about what you have learned and how you feel. This is your fractions reflection!

steps.title: Think First!
steps.owlText: Before we begin, think about everything you know about fractions. What is a half? What is a quarter? What does 'equal parts' mean? What is fair sharing? Think about all the fraction things you have learned!
steps.studentText: What do you know about fractions? Think about halves, quarters, equal parts, and fair sharing.

media.altText: A brain with fraction symbols inside: 1/2, 1/4, equal signs, sharing images
media.fallbackText: A brain with fraction symbols inside: 1/2, 1/4, equal signs, sharing images

interaction.question: Tell me everything you know about fractions. What is a half? What is a quarter? What are equal parts?

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Review all fraction concepts before assessment
steps.owlText: Let us review everything before we start! A half (1/2) is one of two equal parts. A quarter (1/4) is one of four equal parts. Fractions need equal parts — all parts must be the same size. Fair sharing means everyone gets the same amount. Now you are ready!
steps.studentText: Review: 1/2 = one of two equal parts. 1/4 = one of four equal parts. Equal parts = same size. Fair sharing = everyone gets the same.

media.altText: Four review panels: (1) 1/2 shape, (2) 1/4 shape, (3) equal vs unequal, (4) fair sharing. Each with a checkmark.
media.caption: Review: halves, quarters, equal parts, fair sharing.
media.fallbackText: Four review panels: (1) 1/2 shape, (2) 1/4 shape, (3) equal vs unequal, (4) fair sharing. Each with a checkmark.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect all fraction concepts to real life
steps.owlText: Fractions are all around us! When you cut a chapati in half, that is 1/2. When you cut a cake into 4 equal slices, each is 1/4. When you share food fairly with friends, you are using fractions. When you fold paper evenly, you are making fractions. You have learned so much!
steps.studentText: Fractions are everywhere in real life. You have learned to see them in food, paper, sharing, and shapes!

media.altText: Real life collage: chapati half, cake quarters, paper folding, children sharing, shapes with fractions
media.fallbackText: Real life collage: chapati half, cake quarters, paper folding, children sharing, shapes with fractions

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.owlText: Let me show you the kinds of questions you will see. Question: This shape is divided into 2 equal parts. One is shaded. What fraction? Answer: one half (1/2)! Question: A cake is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1. What fraction? Answer: one quarter (1/4)! You know this!
steps.studentText: Assessment questions ask you to: identify fractions from shapes, count equal parts, and solve fair sharing problems. You know how to do all of these!

media.altText: Two example questions with answers: (1) shape showing 1/2 with answer, (2) cake with 4 slices with answer
media.fallbackText: Two example questions with answers: (1) shape showing 1/2 with answer, (2) cake with 4 slices with answer

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Practice assessment-style question: identify fraction from shape
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! This circle is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded? Choose the correct answer.
steps.studentText: This circle is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded?

media.altText: A circle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded.
media.fallbackText: A circle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded.

interaction.question: What fraction is shaded?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! The circle is divided into 2 equal parts and 1 is shaded. That is one half!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Count the equal parts. There are 2. One is shaded. That is one half (1/2).

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Comprehensive assessment question: equal vs unequal (QC-E1)
steps.owlText: Quick check! Which shape shows equal parts? Remember: fractions need parts that are the same size.

media.altText: Four shapes: A has 2 equal parts, B has 2 unequal parts, C has 3 unequal parts, D has 4 unequal parts.
media.fallbackText: Four shapes: A has 2 equal parts, B has 2 unequal parts, C has 3 unequal parts, D has 4 unequal parts.

interaction.question: Which shape shows equal parts?
options: Shape A: rectangle divided into 2 equal parts
Shape B: rectangle divided into 2 unequal parts
Shape C: circle divided into 3 unequal parts
Shape D: square divided into 4 unequal parts
interaction.correctAnswer: Shape A: rectangle divided into 2 equal parts
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Only Shape A has equal parts. Fractions need equal parts!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Remember: fractions need parts that are the same size. Look for the shape where all parts are equal.

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.purpose: Deep reflection on all fraction learning
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about everything you have learned about fractions. You learned about halves, quarters, equal parts, fair sharing, patterns, and more. You are a fractions champion!
steps.studentText: What did you learn about fractions? How do you feel about what you know?

interaction.question: How do you feel about fractions now?
options: 🤔 I know some things, still learning

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You completed your fractions assessment today! You know about halves, quarters, equal parts, fair sharing, and patterns. You are a fractions champion! Keep practicing and looking for fractions everywhere!
steps.studentText: You completed your fractions assessment! You are a fractions champion!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a trophy that says 'Fractions Champion!'
media.fallbackText: Celebration with stars and a trophy that says 'Fractions Champion!'
